title: The Triple Hoop
subtitle: Three arcs of light on the ear, each stone held singly, all moving as one.

stone.origin: The collet is the oldest setting form in fine jewellery — a ring of metal that holds the stone precisely without obscuring it. The Triple Hoop sets 18 diamonds in collets across three continuous arcs: each stone held singly, each entered from every direction, three rows of light that move as one piece on the ear. The collet here is not historical reference; it is the right setting for what these diamonds are asked to do.

description: The collet is the oldest setting in fine jewellery — a ring of metal that grips the stone precisely and then disappears behind it. The Triple Hoop carries eighteen diamonds in collets across three continuous arcs, each stone held on its own, open to light from every direction. Worn, the three rows read as one piece: a single band of brilliance that turns and catches with the head. The setting here is not a historical gesture — it is simply the right way to hold what these stones are asked to do.
